title: read-page manifest
description: Contract of the JSON printed by scripts/readpage.py (schema 1). Documented here, enforced by tests/props.py: a manifest may not use a top-level or sub-field that is missing from this file, so this document cannot quietly drift from the code.

advice.description: one sentence, the single next step

dir.description: the folder the artefacts are in

restored.description: blocks of page.md the extractor dropped that were put back in place

outside.description: bytes of page.md still outside the text: menus, link lists, fragments, banners

signals.description: status_reason is set by the code for every normal answer (including a crash); it is not required here so an older entry still validates.

browser_waited.description: networkidle | mount:<selector> | body - the extra wait that produced the text, empty when the first pass had it

partial.description: the transfer was cut (a timeout or a broken connection): the text may stop early

render_error.description: the browser showed its own error page (ERR_..., HTTP ERROR 503); its text was not used

browser_blocked.description: requests of a public page to the local network or a non-web scheme that the browser was not allowed to make

browser_inside.description: where a public page's browser reached into the local network through a redirect (host:port) on a machine whose own proxy keeps netguard aside; its text was not used, and the advice names the flag that reads the page another way

images_reused.description: pictures taken by a hard link from another page of the same host

images_outside.description: pictures of the page the text does not show (menus, footers); page.md has them

rescued_after.description: the text is a reader's or the archive's because the live page did not answer ("no answer") or answered 5xx ("HTTP 503"); the cache keeps such an answer 60 s, not 15 minutes

no_transcript.description: a video address without subtitles: why, and the page itself was read as a page

ocr_timeouts.description: pages whose OCR did not finish in time; the text marks the gap, the other pages are kept

env_failed.description: the skill's own environment (readpage.py --setup) has a Python that started and ended before the read began: why; this read ran in the machine's Python

ocr_error.description: OCR is installed and does not start (tesserocr: a path it cannot open, a pack cut short): why; the answer names it as missing: ocr

tables.description: a PDF's tables, laid out by the layout model, for every PDF of the read (the PDF itself, the PDFs of a ZIP, an archived copy; one 10 s a read for them all): the pages where a table stands as Markdown, how many tables, the model's seconds, the pages of the document, and `left` - pages that look like a table and were not laid out: the time a read has ran out (--download lays them all out), a page was too heavy for it (`heavy`), or the model stopped (`error`). Said also when the model was asked and kept nothing. With --alternate (`markdown`) the model lays out the document as Markdown, and `left` names the pages that stayed PyMuPDF's text

pages.description: page numbers from 1 as ranges, as the advice writes them: "2, 8-9, 28-600"

left.description: page numbers from 1 as ranges, as the advice writes them: "2, 8-9, 28-600"

heavy.description: of `left`, the pages too heavy for a read's time (over 8 000 vector paths, or 2 000 words in one block of text): not asked, except with --download

more.description: after the time ran out, pages were judged by their text alone: one with rulings only may look like a table and not be named

error.description: why the model did not work: it does not load here (pymupdf4llm needs onnxruntime), its process ended - the pages from there are in `left` - or a page failed (the other pages are still asked)

markdown.description: --alternate: the pages are pymupdf4llm's Markdown, not the tables step's

files.description: the PDFs inside a ZIP: each one's name, pages laid out, pages left (and too heavy), tables and pages

pages.description: page numbers from 1 as ranges, as the advice writes them: "2, 8-9, 28-600"

left.description: page numbers from 1 as ranges, as the advice writes them: "2, 8-9, 28-600"

heavy.description: page numbers from 1 as ranges, as the advice writes them: "2, 8-9, 28-600"

screenshot_tiles_needed.description: how many tiles the page has, when fewer were returned than that

override.description: --force-external sent a URL that may carry a secret

conflict.description: which flag met which rule: ["force_external wins", "secret heuristic ignored"] or ["force_external refused", "internal host"]

images.description: the text's pictures in the order they appear, then those of page.md or --download; the number is the marker's and the file's

n.description: #n in the marker [img #n · ...] and the NN- of the file

in.description: text: in content.md; page: page.md or --download only; list: a document's picture with no place in the text

file.description: img/NN-words.ext; absent when it was not downloaded

why.description: why there is no file: 404, timeout, no time (N s), refused: ..., --deny-images

failed_at.description: when the network failed it (Unix seconds): an answer printed PICTURE_RETRY_AFTER (30 s) later asks it once more

retried.description: it failed again when asked once more: it is not asked again

reused.description: taken from another page of the same host instead of the network

revalidated.description: --refresh asked with the validators and the server answered 304: the file was kept

order.description: a document's picture: its place in document.xml or the EPUB spine

screenshots.description: the page as 1280 px wide tiles, never scaled; N is how many were asked for

ignored.description: this call's arguments that are not read-page's flags, or values it cannot use: left out, the read went on; only in --json output, never in the saved manifest

ocr.description: --ocr N only (never in the saved manifest): picture N, how its text was read, or why not
